title: VSift visual candidate, brief view v1
description: One visual candidate as the brief view of candidates gives it (--view brief, 0.2.1): the identity, representative_us, span, reasons, stability, the size of the change that opened it and the visual_hash that shows when a screen repeats, which is what a reader needs to place it and to decide whether to look at its frame. It is NOT an evidence record: the evidence stream always carries visual-candidate.schema.json, whose record an index stores by candidate_id, and a brief view is refused for a stream. Every member is the member of the same name of the full candidate, with the same value. The brief view leaves out what every candidate of the index repeats (source_id, source_segment_id, stream_index, displayed_dimensions and analysis: the answer's item_constants hold them once), the window (its ordinal is representative_us divided by the index's window_us, rounded down), and change_window and sample_count, which the full view still gives. change is absent, not null, for a first frame or a periodic sample, which no change opened. Candidates are evidence assistance, not evidence: the original frames are authoritative.

candidate_id.description: Derived from the session, source, stream, analysis profile, window and representative time, so it never changes when later windows are analysed.

reasons.description: Why the candidate was proposed, as visual-candidate.schema.json defines each reason.

change.description: The size of the change that opened the candidate, as visual-candidate.schema.json defines it; absent when no observed change opened it.

visual_hash.description: A 64-bit difference hash of the representative frame as 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits: a similarity key that shows when a screen repeats, not a security digest.
